title: an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver
intention: A component that receives a request it cannot fill raises the trouble at its own address, under an identity naming what was asked, counted on every repeat, and tells the caller which trouble it raised; a sender blocked by the refusal adds to that same trouble rather than writing its own. The test before raising stays the outline's: can only CC or Akien fix this? If not, it is a log line, not a trouble (outline 3.4.3.4-5).
why: Ruling 8h, 2026-10-05, Akien verbatim: "Any component that gets a request that it can't fill, that's a trouble ticket. We will eventually class certain classes of trouble is not requiring a ticket. Because like if we throw a trouble ticket because I mistype something on the Cairn command line, that might not be a trouble that I actually need to go look at.  But every requester that gets something they can't do should throw a ticket. Because we need to stop people throwing things at them that they can't do." The lived symptom: codemother asked inference_domain for a 'codemother' domain row that does not exist about 1,000 times a day, and every ask was refused in silence, so nobody could see the broken caller. This is spanning: every receiver implements it at its own boundary, so no one directory can hold it.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth): a refused request today is silent at the receiver. CP4 via Telos: the lived symptom is a component spending ~1000 refusals a day on a caller nobody can see. Ruling 8h, 2026-10-05.
how: Two children, each proved before this parent. e9a2d8ae7d43 (PROVED): inference_domain raises inference-unfilled-domain-<asked> when a domain row does not exist, the codemother case. eff2fb9810de: BaseShim's _bounce_to_sender raises the trouble at the receiving shim under the identity the bounce already carries, so every device's undeliverable mail is raised where it failed; handle_bounce's existing raise under that identity is the sender's addition, which the trouble lane folds into the same trouble. Then the piece is written at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver.md quoting 8h and Akien's answer open-b9037ca75019 verbatim and naming each child.
falsifier: GREEN when (a) each child's receiver raises one trouble per unfillable request it fails, the same identity on a repeat and a different one for a different ask, naming the caller; (b) the refusal or bounce the caller gets is unchanged and names the trouble, even when the trouble lane is down; (c) a fillable request raises nothing; (d) the sender's raise under the bounce's identity folds into the receiver's trouble, not beside it. RED if any receiver refuses in silence or the trouble replaces the refusal. WRONG INTENT if a failure only a typist can fix (a cairn CLI typo) becomes a trouble rather than a log line. Horizon: the codemother 'codemother' domain asks show as one counted trouble at inference_domain.

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: the children are proved first, one per component boundary (RULE 1). Each raises at its receiver through raise_trouble (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py), with an identity naming what was asked (the fold on identity is the counter) and a detail naming the caller. The caller's refusal is unchanged.

D2: SETTLED by Akien's answer open-b9037ca75019: the receiver raises and reports to the caller, and the sender appends ('writing is not safe, but appending is'). BaseShim's receiver raise is child eff2fb9810de; handle_bounce's raise under the same identity stays as the append.
D3: SETTLED by open-7d7bcae62287 (the outline stands, 3.4.3.5): the test runs before raising, so no no-ticket seam is built; a failure only its typist can fix is a log line at its own surface.

D4: SETTLED: at BUILDME the piece is written at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver.md, quoting 8h verbatim and the answer to open-b9037ca75019 verbatim and naming each child's address. It is then compiled into the lab through cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh.
